title: Constant Down-Right Diagonals
statement:
You get a grid of integers grid with m rows and n columns. A down-right diagonal is a run of cells where each next cell is one row down and one column right.

Return true if every down-right diagonal holds one value repeated along its whole length, and false otherwise.

examples.why: Each row is the row above shifted one step right: diagonals read 9; 5,5; 4,4,4; 7,7; 2.
The main diagonal reads 1, 1, 9. All other diagonals are fine, so you must check right up to the last cell.
The diagonal starting at row 1 reads 3, 8.

hints: You do not need to walk each diagonal separately. Which single neighbour must each cell match?
A cell and the cell up-left of it are on the same diagonal.
For every cell not in the first row or first column, compare it with grid[i − 1][j − 1]. Any mismatch means false.

explain.intuition:
A diagonal is constant exactly when every pair of neighbouring cells on it is equal. Each cell's up-left neighbour is its predecessor on the same diagonal. So instead of tracing diagonals, compare every cell with the cell at [i − 1][j − 1]. If all those pairs match, every diagonal is constant.

This also streams nicely: you only ever need the previous row, which matters if the grid is too big to load at once.
steps: Loop over rows i from 1 to m − 1 and columns j from 1 to n − 1.
pitfalls: Comparing with grid[i − 1][j + 1], which checks the other diagonal direction.
Starting the loops at 0 and reading index −1. In JavaScript that gives undefined and a silent wrong answer.
Checking only diagonals that start in the first row and forgetting those that start in the first column.

solutions.title: Trace every diagonal
solutions.idea: Start a walk at each cell of the first row and first column and check that all cells along it equal the first one.

solutions.title: Compare with the up-left neighbour
solutions.idea: Each cell must equal the cell diagonally above it. One pass, no bookkeeping.

followups: The grid is stored on disk and you can load only one row into memory at a time. How do you check it?
You can load only part of a row at a time. What changes?
